- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged mean.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope or add 0.5–1.0 unit bias toward true direction.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >2σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.00” values, model underperforms; add 0.5–1.0 unit upward bias to compensate for low sentiment drag.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is >10% below forecast, check if sentiment was negative; if so, model may be overly conservative; adjust upward by 1–2%.
- If forecast is consistently 2–3% below true outcome over 3–5 consecutive days, model is underestimating; add 0.5–1.0 unit upward bias unless sentiment is negative.
